summary: Crash after attempting to move item from off-hand in Creative inventory
description: A crash is caused when trying to offhand an item in the creative inventory after attempting to do so in the search tab Steps to reproduce: - Have an item in your off-hand in creative mode - Open inventory and go to the Search tab - Use the off-hand key to try and put the item in your off-hand into the hotbar (stopped as the search box takes priority) - Change back to the Survival Inventory tab, and then press the off-hand key again without hovering cursor over any inventory slots or: - Have an item in your off-hand in creative mode - Hover over any empty slot in a tab other than Survival Inventory - Select the Survival Inventory tab, and then press the off-hand key without hovering cursor over any inventory slots As far as I can tell (Not a programmer or anything, didn t look at code, just from my small testing) this happens because the offhand hotkey when pressed tries to put the item in your offhand into the last inventory slot that you had "selected" (hovered over) with your cursor. When you try to use the offhand hotkey when under the search tab, the search box takes priority and types instead of allowing you to offhand, making it the last selected inventory "slot" (I believe,) when you change back to your player inventory tab, there s no textbox anymore, so when you try to use the hotkey again, the game crashes as there s no "last selected" slot to offhand to (or maybe because it tries to offhand to the textbox? I dunno I m not a programmer) Simply hovering over an inventory slot after swapping to the player inventory before using the offhand hotkey will prevent the crash and allow the hotkey to work as normal.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Ensure you are in Creative mode.
2. Have an item in your off-hand slot.
3. Open the inventory and navigate to the Search tab.
4. Attempt to use the off-hand key to move the item into the hotbar (this will be prevented as the search box takes priority).
5. Change back to the Survival Inventory tab without hovering over any inventory slots.
6. Press the off-hand key again while not hovering over any inventory slots.
7. Observe that the game crashes.

Alternatively, follow these steps:

1. Ensure you are in Creative mode.
2. Have an item in your off-hand slot.
3. Open the inventory and navigate to a tab other than Survival Inventory.
4. Hover over any empty slot within this tab.
5. Select the Survival Inventory tab without hovering over any slots.
6. Press the off-hand key while not hovering over any inventory slots.
7. Observe that the game crashes.
Observed Behavior: In the described scenario, when attempting to move an item from the off-hand into the hotbar while in Creative mode, a crash occurs under specific conditions. To reproduce this issue, start with an item in your off-hand and open the inventory, navigating to the Search tab. Attempting to use the off-hand key will be prevented by the search box taking priority, thus not allowing you to move the item into the hotbar. After switching back to the Survival Inventory tab without hovering over any inventory slots, pressing the off-hand key again results in a crash. This behavior also occurs if you hover over an empty slot in another tab before selecting the Survival Inventory and then pressing the off-hand key. The issue likely stems from the game attempting to place the item into the last selected inventory slot, which is nullified when switching tabs or due to the search box taking priority. Hovering over any inventory slot after changing tabs can prevent the crash by providing a valid target for the off-hand action.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to move an item from the off-hand to the hotbar in the Creative inventory, the game should successfully transfer the item without crashing. This should work regardless of whether you previously used the Search tab or hovered over different slots. The action should not be affected by the last selected slot or any text boxes, ensuring a smooth transition of items between the off-hand and hotbar.
